messages:
emma: Heads-up — Acme says a subset of streaming calls are failing with a client-side 'broken pipe' and we're showing them as 5xx in billing. They pasted a curl repro and logs. trace_id=tr-8f3a

emma: Repro curl they ran:```bash
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream' \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REPLACE' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"prompt":"<long prompt>","stream":true}'
```

jordan: ack — putting on SRE queue. Any sample gateway log lines?

emma: pasted proxy snippet from customer side (redacted):```
[2026-03-10T18:21:03Z] proxy: upstream write error: broken pipe (EPIPE) while sending chunk
[2026-03-10T18:21:03Z] proxy: upstream returned premature eof: chunked-terminator-missing
[2026-03-10T18:21:03Z] gateway: classified response as 5xx, status_code=502, trace=tr-8f3a
```

li: thanks. quick hypothesis: client is closing the TCP connection before we wrote the final chunk/trailer; our gateway currently marks that as upstream failure -> 5xx. We should classify it as client-abort to avoid billing.

noah: I remember we added a conservative rule that treated upstream half-close without final chunk as 5xx because of a couple of real upstream errors. But that causes noisy billing for streaming clients that abort mid-stream.

emma: Acme wants credits for ~120 calls across a 24h window. They can reproduce with their editor extension which cancels when user types.

jordan: steps I'll take: 1) pull full trace + tcp dump for tr-8f3a 2) surface sample to infra 3) create temporary billing exemption for Acme while we triage.

li: repro in-house: small Node script that opens request and destroys socket after receiving N tokens. Patch:```js
const req = http.request(opts);
req.write(payload);
req.on('data', (chunk) => {
  if (++count === 3) req.socket.destroy(); // simulate client abort
});
```
We see gateway logs identical to customer's.

noah: good repro. I ran a canary with a change to classification logic: if connection has local socket FIN (client closed) within 2s of last chunk and upstream returned partial chunk set, tag as client_abort rather than 5xx. Canary on us-east-1 for 10% looks clean.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/classify-client-abort -> service/gateway (canary 10%)

emma: can we also avoid counting those requests for billing retroactively for that time window? CS wants a list to present to billing.

jordan: I'll assemble a trace list query: filter trace_id where status=5xx and proto=stream and tcp_flag=RST/FIN and created_by=client. That should pull the ~120.

li: PR ready (https://git.internal/pr/9876) — classification + metric delta. Unit tests cover chunked streams where trailer absent and socket closed by client.

noah: note — edge case: some real upstream errors still present where server never wrote final chunk due to crash; we should not hide those entirely. The new rule differentiates by tcp side (client vs upstream) and time delta.

emma: awesome. I'll update Acme and grant provisional credit pending final audit. CS ticket: CS-4321.

jordan: leaving a follow-up item: add a realtime alert for surge in client_aborts to detect buggy client releases.

li: will merge PR after canary completes (in ~30m).

emma: thanks all — will post resolution to customer and close escalation when billing adjustment is confirmed. :raised_hands:
